human_tolerance.notes: Gregarious in flocks of 15-20 birds, larger flocks of up to 100 not being unusual, and non-migratory; it visits fruiting trees in parks, streets and gardens across its range and builds communal nest cavities in termite nests.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Clutches of about 11 eggs with about 7 young reaching adulthood; nests are built in communal cavities in termite nests.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Non-migratory; moves in flocks between fruiting trees.

vocalizations.description: A harsh, strident, squawk repeated by the whole flock in flight, so that a passing group sounds continuous.
A sharp, excited screeching given when the flock is disturbed or mobbing a predator.

taxonomy.note: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy gives Aves Psittaciformes Psittacidae and the authorship on the matched name; the Wikidata item confirms the English common name.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2479562 and iNaturalist taxon id 19214 as matched by the GBIF backbone and the iNaturalist taxa API; Wikidata Q1086851 carries the same identifiers.

common_names.note: English common name from Wikidata; Portuguese name from the article's interlanguage links.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern for Plain parakeet.

range.note: Wikipedia: endemic to Brazil, ranging from Bahia to Parana and as far inland as Goias. Native range listed as BR.

traits.body_plan.note: A perching passerine or parrot; biped_winged mesh.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs; wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Authored params for the shared perching-songbird program. Climb is the declared non-flight locomotion and has no pose in schema/v0.1/body-plans.json, so no climb pose is declared; a long flee distance suits a flock that flushes together.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None; the young hatch as fledged nestlings.

traits.senses.note: Colour vision in all birds; hearing and olfaction values are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them here.

traits.nest_type.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the communal nest cavity in a termite nest from the Portuguese Wikipedia article; the perch weight is judgement.

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Mass 63 g; Wikipedia gives about 63 g.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Fruit 30, Diet-Seed 30, Diet-PlantO 30 (plant other mapped to browse), Diet-Inv 10.

traits.social.note: Portuguese Wikipedia: gregarious, flocks of 15-20 birds with larger flocks of up to 100 not unusual. group_size [2, 20] uses the typical flock as the upper bound.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0 (diurnal); Plain parakeet describes daytime activity.

traits.defense.note: Authored: flies to cover when disturbed.

traits.wariness.note: Authored. Bold and noisy in city parks and streets, so set low.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-canopy 60, ForStrat-midhigh 20, ForStrat-understory 20 (canopy, midhigh and understory mapped to arboreal); the ground share is judgement, for feeding on the ground below fruiting trees.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: roosts in dense vegetation or a cavity.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the communal nest cavity in a termite nest from the Portuguese Wikipedia article; the perch weight is judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Portuguese Wikipedia describes it as one of the most invasive of all bird species because of its nest-building, and as a pest even within its native range; it is non-migratory and flocks visit fruiting trees.

seasonal.strategy.note: A year-round resident of subtropical Brazil with no migration or dormancy described.

seasonal.phases.note: Clutch size and nesting from the Portuguese Wikipedia article; the windows are judgements.

behavior.note: Authored params for the shared perching-songbird program. Climb is the declared non-flight locomotion and has no pose in schema/v0.1/body-plans.json, so no climb pose is declared; a long flee distance suits a flock that flushes together.

look.note: Colours from the Wikipedia description (green body and underparts, orange-tinged forehead and breast, pale horn bill); proportions authored for a small parakeet with a long pointed tail.

traits.wingspan_m.note: AVONET Wing.Length 113.4 mm is the wing chord; multiplied by 2.80, the passerine ratio this repository's own sourced thrush record (species/turdus-merula) gives. A parrot's rounded wing gives a shorter span for the same chord, so this is the least certain of the six wingspans here and is an upper-ish estimate, not a measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No openly licensed source states a wild lifespan for this species. Authored as a low-precision value typical of a small parakeet, whose captive and wild longevity both run to many years; it is a judgement, not a measurement.

vocalizations.song.note: Call description from the Plain parakeet article; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Call description from the Plain parakeet article; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them.
